edges.effect_quant: In genotype-defined low-MTHFR-activity lymphoblastoid cell lines (n=35), folic acid failed to raise intracellular 5-methyltetrahydrofolate whereas direct 5-methyltetrahydrofolate exposure increased intracellular 5-methyltetrahydrofolate about 10-fold; in a 220-woman randomized trial of recurrent miscarriage with MTHFR polymorphisms, 5-methyltetrahydrofolate raised serum folate more than folic acid but did not reduce abortion rates.
edges.population: people with reduced MTHFR activity, especially women of childbearing age and recurrent-miscarriage cohorts with MTHFR polymorphisms
edges.mechanism: 5-methyltetrahydrofolate is the bioactive folate form downstream of the MTHFR step, so it can theoretically bypass reduced enzymatic conversion in C677T carriers. That should improve intracellular folate handling and reduce unmetabolized folic acid exposure, even if downstream clinical benefit is not always demonstrable.
edges.summary: Activated folate has a plausible pharmacologic advantage for MTHFR 677TT-related physiology because it bypasses the impaired conversion step and improves some biochemical folate measures. Clinical superiority over folic acid, however, remains modest and inconsistent, so the edge is best treated as a low-confidence protective option rather than a settled outcome-changing intervention.
edges.caveats: Much of the support is mechanistic or based on biochemical endpoints, and the main genotype-aware miscarriage RCT did not show a clear advantage for hard pregnancy outcomes. This edge should therefore be interpreted more as a targeted supplementation rationale than as proof of major clinical benefit in all C677TT carriers.
